setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep opened with 'you spoke with Kim two days ago, something like that... So he briefed me in on where you're at right now', and the prospect corroborated it independently twice: 'I was telling Kim that I was really into it for like two years and I just kept getting injured.'

prospect.name: Kyle
prospect.location: Pennsylvania, USA, about an hour from Baltimore. Born and raised in Arizona, then lived in Texas.
prospect.occupation: Quality control inspector at a manufacturer of oil, hydraulic and aerospace filtration filters, working ten-hour shifts from 5am to around 3:20pm, seated most of the day. Simultaneously studying for an STCW certification at a maritime institute in Baltimore, aiming to work for Navy Sealift Command on a three-year government contract as a civilian.
prospect.family_status: Lives with a roommate. No partner or children mentioned.
prospect.training_background: Trained consistently in a gym for about two years and stopped roughly three years ago because of recurring injury. Warmed up and stretched before and after every session and was mocked for it by friends. Returned to the gym about three weeks before this call and describes the comeback as tough — 'I'm lifting weights, and I'm like, man, this is barely anything, and I'm incredibly sore the next day.' Walks and hikes regularly and used to boulder every weekend in Texas, plus 20-mile trail rides; has found no climbing gym since moving to Pennsylvania. No kettlebell experience; has been following Trevor's content for about a month.
prospect.medical: Recurrent left shoulder injury with associated trapezius and neck pain, flaring roughly every one to two months across two years of training. Never imaged and never clinically assessed — asked directly whether he had had an x-ray or any test done he answered 'No, I never did.' Managed by icing, avoiding all shoulder work, and waiting two weeks to a month for the pain to settle, at which point it typically returned within days. No surgery. Reports no pain at all in the three years since he stopped training. Reports no current stiffness or movement limitation. Sleeps roughly seven to seven and a half hours, in bed by 8-9pm and up at 4am, on a new mattress. Sluggish mornings; has been using energy drinks heavily and reports brain fog, though a self-run month without them produced no noticeable difference. Heavy snacker — potato chips and office candy.

signals: Lost ground to a defined bad season — a two-year injury cycle that ended training altogether: 'I got tired of it, man. I got tired of feeling in pain all the time.'
Wants a former self back and names it concretely: 'I do want to get my abs back. I haven't seen my abs in a couple of years. I've been in hibernation.'

Carries audible regret about the length of the gap, discovering it live on the call: 'I think it might actually have been coming on three years now that I stopped working out. That's bad now that I think about that.'
Not the_medically_constrained: no clinician has ruled anything out and no assessment has ever been sought — the injury is self-managed and undiagnosed.
Not the_optimizer: no price tolerance at all, and the baseline is three years detrained rather than good.

goals.text: Find a strength programme he can sustain for longevity without getting injured — 'someone I can do 10 years from now and still feel great'
Stop the injury cycle — 'I'm tired of being injured'
Get his abs back after three years
Build a strong core, which he has already noticed reduces his back and shoulder pain
Regain the confidence and energy he had when he trained — 'I felt more confident, I had more energy'
Stop feeling stiff — 'I want to actually have mobility'
Avoid gaining weight now that he sits down all day
Get back to bouldering and long trail rides
Get off energy drinks and out of the morning brain fog
Cook at home again and stop buying food out

pains.text: Recurrent left shoulder and trap injury every one to two months across two years, never diagnosed or imaged
Quit training entirely for three years because of the injury cycle — 'I was like, well, I don't feel pain anymore, so this is kind of nice to not wake up and be in pain'
Sedentary ten-hour shifts starting at 5am, with a 4am alarm
Heavy snacking with no self-control around office candy — 'I don't have like self-control. When I see that, it's just like, especially if it's Reese's cups'
Energy drink dependence and brain fog despite proving to himself he does not need the caffeine
Stopped cooking at home since he stopped training, and now buys most food out
Paying tuition out of pocket with $2,100 due in August
Roughly $300 of monthly surplus and a single credit card with a $300 limit
Lost his hobbies to relocation — no bouldering gym and little hiking since moving to Pennsylvania
Uncertain whether his technique is what keeps injuring him and has no way to find out

objections.raw_quote: Oh wow, okay. I don't think I have that right now, to be honest with you. I didn't know it was gonna be that much. Is there any way that I can do like payments or how is it working?
objections.rep_response: Named the upfront credit card norm, immediately conceded it would not work here, then took a financial picture — monthly surplus, credit cards and limits, savings — and paused the call to text an owner or supervisor for options: 'I need to reach out to someone. You know, I'm not the owner. So I don't have all the possibilities here.'

objections.raw_quote: To be honest with you, I wouldn't be able to because I got to pay my tuition. It's like $2,100 and I have to pay that in August.
objections.rep_response: Moved down the ladder to a six-month split quoted at about $1,200 per month.

objections.raw_quote: Let's be honest with you, Andrew, I won't be able to do that. That's way more than I was comfortable with spending. I would love to, but yeah, man, that's too much for me right now.
objections.rep_response: Introduced third-party financing through Pava, comparing it to Klarna and disclosing that interest would apply, and sent the application link live. The application was declined: 'we're sorry we're unable to offer a payment plan at this time.' The rep suspected a technical fault, re-sent by email, and it was declined again on the laptop.

objections.raw_quote: If I'm being completely honest, I don't think I'll be able to do that either. I'd love to, man. I really would.
objections.rep_response: Cut the scope — offered a three-month programme at $4,000 with the option to top up to the full $6,000 later — and when that was also declined verbally, proposed running the Pava application again against the smaller amount.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Four structures were offered in descending order over about twenty minutes, all after a live text escalation to an owner or supervisor. (1) $6,000 upfront on a credit card. (2) 50/50 — '3K now and 3K in 30 days', stated as interest-free. (3) A six-month split quoted at 'about $1,200 per month', which totals $7,200 rather than $6,000, with no explanation of the difference. (4) Pava third-party financing over up to twelve months with interest acknowledged — declined twice by the underwriter, on phone and then on laptop. Finally a three-month programme at $4,000 with a top-up path to six months, also to be run through Pava. Nothing was agreed.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Asserted without terms: 'the whole program, it takes six months. Like that's the amount he needs for a full transformation. And there's a guarantee.'

prospect_financials.note: About $300 a month put into savings while studying. One credit card with a $300 total limit and no others. Asked whether savings were four or five figures he answered 'It's, no, it's like, it's like five, yeah' — recorded as stated, but it sits oddly against a $300 monthly surplus and a $2,100 tuition bill he cannot cover alongside anything else, so treat it as unreliable. Tuition of $2,100 due in August. A third-party lender declined him twice during the call.

evidence: The recording truncates mid-transaction at 01:00:08 with the rep asking for a screenshot of the second declined financing application, so the final result is not on tape.
Nothing was paid, nothing was agreed, and no follow-up call or time was booked before the recording ends.

Every structure offered was declined: $6,000 upfront ('I don't think I have that right now'), 50/50 ('I wouldn't be able to because I got to pay my tuition'), six months at ~$1,200 ('that's way more than I was comfortable with spending'), and the three-month $4,000 tier ('I don't think I'll be able to do that either').

Third-party financing was declined twice by the underwriter — 'we're sorry we're unable to offer a payment plan at this time' — first on his phone, then again on his laptop after the rep re-sent it by email.

Counter-evidence keeping this out of 'lost': intent was unusually high and never withdrawn — 'I would love to be a part of the program' and 'I'd love to, man. I really would' — and the rep was still actively working a third application against the smaller amount when the tape ends.
On the balance of what is recorded this was heading to lost on affordability; it is scored undetermined only because the deciding event, a credit decision, happens after the recording stops.
outcome.next_step: Unknown. The last recorded action is the rep asking for a screenshot of the declined Pava application and preparing to send a fresh link for the three-month $4,000 amount. No follow-up was scheduled on tape.

notable.note: Three things a principal should see. First, the six-month instalment was quoted at 'about $1,200 per month', which is $7,200 against a $6,000 price, with no surcharge or interest mentioned — either an arithmetic error told to a prospect as a price, or an undisclosed premium. Second, a prospect whose entire training history is a recurring, never-diagnosed shoulder injury was asked directly whether he had ever had it imaged, answered no, and was then taken through an overhead-loaded kettlebell programme with no suggestion that he get it assessed first; the rep's answer to the injury was video form checks. Third, and most costly commercially: this prospect has about $300 a month and a $300 credit limit, and Primal University exists at $199 a month, cancel anytime — the same rep offered it to a Dutch prospect the day before against a €200 ceiling — and it was never mentioned here. Instead he was walked down a ladder from $6,000 to $4,000 and pushed twice through a consumer lender that declined him. Also of note for the payment-policy picture: terms are not fixed and are cleared live by text with an owner mid-call — 'I need to reach out to someone. You know, I'm not the owner. So I don't have all the possibilities here.'

quality.notes: Persistent inversion throughout, with several long passages fully swapped — the rep's own hip-condition story at 00:19:56 to 00:22:33 alternates attribution almost line by line, and the entire nutrition presentation and the price statement are attributed to the prospect. Role was resolved from content. The prospect's phone connection dropped audio at least twice around 00:41:34. The recording is truncated: it stops mid-exchange at 01:00:08 with no sign-off, while a financing screenshot was being requested, so the outcome of the call is not recoverable from this file. The prospect appears only as 'Kyle'; a surname is not stated, though the rep reads back an email address at 00:51:51 that implies one.
